chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the musk of the Kaaba that touches the garment of the Muhrim (one in Ihram), he said: 'There is no harm with it and he should not wash it, for it is pure.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim's Ihram clothing gets stained with the musk of the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the musk used to perfume the Kaaba is ritually pure (tahur), meaning its transfer to a pilgrim's garment does not invalidate the Ihram state nor require washing. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the physical purity of the substance and the ritual state of the pilgrim, emphasizing that minor, non-intentional contact with pure scents does not disrupt the sanctity of the pilgrimage rites.
